content.title: About
content.content: Sun-dried tomatoes are ripe tomatoes that have been dried in the sun or a dehydrator until most of the moisture is removed. They have a concentrated sweet‑tart flavor, a dense chewy texture, and a vivid red color. Sun-dried tomatoes are a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, used in salads, pastas, pizzas, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional production occurs in Mediterranean regions where the climate allows natural dehydration.
Sugar content can reach up to 30 % of their weight, making them naturally sweet without added sugar.
They are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after drying.
Sun-dried tomatoes are often packed in oil with herbs, extending shelf life and adding flavor.
In Italy they are called “pomodori secchi” and feature in classic dishes such as pasta with anchovies.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium contribute to normal blood pressure and cardiac function.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many dried fruits, sun-dried tomatoes contain little fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Many sun-dried tomatoes are salted; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Sugar concentration
items.content: The high natural sugar can raise blood glucose levels; diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Contamination risk if improperly dried
items.content: Insufficient drying temperatures can allow microbial growth. Purchase from reputable producers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sun-dried tomatoes can be eaten as a snack, added to salads, pastas, risottos, pizzas, omelets, or blended into sauces. Soaking them in olive oil with herbs enhances flavor and softness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sun-dried tomatoes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. When packed in oil, keep refrigerated and use within 2‑3 weeks. Dried‑only tomatoes last up to 6 months in a dry environment. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.
